succeeded cleanly, same 6 projects as the direct curl read — corroborates Pages read via the actual tool #348 would use, not just raw curl.

calls.step: GET https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/tokens (attempt to read the token's OWN policy, to settle Pages Edit-vs-Read-only directly)
calls.result: "Unauthorized to access requested resource" (code 9109). Expected/normal boundary — reading a token's own policy needs a separate 'API Tokens: Read' permission, which security-conscious deploy tokens routinely omit. This 403 is NOT evidence against Pages:Edit; it answers a different question (can this token read Cloudflare's token-management API at all — no).

grantsFoundVsNeeded.Zone -> DNS -> Read (mvox.eu): CONFIRMED FOUND — dns_records:read in the zone's own permissions array + live DNS-record read succeeded
grantsFoundVsNeeded.Zone -> DNS -> Edit (mvox.eu): CONFIRMED FOUND — dns_records:edit in the zone's own permissions array (Cloudflare-reported, most decisive signal available; not inferred from a successful write, since none was attempted)
grantsFoundVsNeeded.Account -> Cloudflare Pages -> Read: CONFIRMED FOUND — project list/direct-read/domains-read all 200, corroborated via both curl and wrangler pages project list
grantsFoundVsNeeded.Account -> Cloudflare Pages -> Edit: CANNOT TELL — Cloudflare's Pages API does not echo a per-resource permissions array the way the Zones API does, so no read-only Pages call can confirm or rule out Edit. The one avenue that WOULD answer directly (reading the token's own configured policy via GET /user/tokens) is itself blocked (403, a distinct and separate permission gap, not itself informative about Pages:Edit). Per the hard fence, no POST/PATCH was attempted to disambiguate.

verdict: MIXED, precisely: Zone->DNS->Edit and Zone->DNS->Read on mvox.eu are CONFIRMED SUFFICIENT (Cloudflare's own permissions array is decisive). Account->Cloudflare Pages->Read is CONFIRMED SUFFICIENT. Account->Cloudflare Pages->Edit is CANNOT TELL — no read-only Cloudflare endpoint can confirm or rule it out; the only test that would settle it is an actual write (POST/PATCH a Pages custom domain), which is out of scope for this probe by the hard fence. Three of four needed grants are confirmed present; the fourth (Pages Edit specifically) is the one genuine unknown, with the exact blocking mechanism named above.
nothingMutated: Every call in this probe was an HTTP GET (plus two read-only wrangler CLI list/whoami invocations, neither of which mutates). No create, update, or delete was issued against any Cloudflare resource at any point. No interactive wrangler login/OAuth flow was invoked.
